crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Drafting Proposals from Past Work
children.blurb: Drafting proposals from past work covers the practice of turning completed research, publications, and project reports into new funding applications.

children.name: Funder Formatting and Compliance
children.blurb: Funder formatting and compliance is the work of matching a proposal to a specific funder's required structure, page limits, font and margin rules, budget forms, certifications, and submission portal checks.

children.name: Budgets and Allowable Costs
children.blurb: Budgets and allowable costs in AI research grant proposals cover the direct and indirect expenses a funder will reimburse, including personnel, equipment, data acquisition, cloud compute, and institutional overhead.

children.name: Finding Collaborators
children.blurb: Finding collaborators in grant proposals and funding means identifying researchers whose expertise, data, or institutional role can strengthen a proposal.

children.name: Predicting Proposal Success
children.blurb: Predicting proposal success uses machine learning to estimate the likelihood that a grant application will be funded, based on proposal text, applicant history, funder priorities, and past review patterns.

sections.body: This field covers the practical work of getting AI research funded. Artificial intelligence is now used to draft proposal text from prior papers, check formatting against agency rules, estimate budgets, suggest collaborators, and score likely success. The pages here describe tools and methods that do these tasks, not theoretical possibilities. Drafting from past work means taking an existing paper and turning its methods and results into a proposal narrative. Compliance checking compares a document to a funder's page limits, font rules, and required sections. Budget tools flag costs that a specific agency will not allow.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Drafting from past work is fairly reliable for producing a first draft, but it still needs a human to fix the argument and match the call. Compliance checking is mostly solved for simple formatting rules, yet agency-specific language and hidden requirements remain hard. Budget estimation works for standard cost categories, but indirect cost rules and institutional policies vary too much for full automation. Finding collaborators is possible through publication and grant databases, but the suggestions are only as good as the data and often miss early career researchers. Predicting proposal success is the least mature, because review outcomes depend on panel dynamics and luck, not just text features.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages move from reusing your own work to checking it, costing it, staffing it, and guessing its odds. Drafting Proposals from Past Work is the starting point for turning a finished paper into a proposal narrative. Funder Formatting and Compliance is where you check that the draft meets a specific agency's rules. Budgets and Allowable Costs helps you build a cost plan that an agency will accept. Finding Collaborators is for adding co-investigators or partners when the call requires a team. Predicting Proposal Success is the last step, where you estimate how competitive the proposal is before submitting. A reader would go to each page in that order, though the compliance and budget pages are often used together.
